newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Morocco's privatisation bonds lift bourse slightly.
newsitem.headline: Morocco's privatisation bonds lift bourse slightly.

text.p: The stock exchange closed 0.13 percent higher on Thursday after receiving a boost from privatisation bonds, stockbrokers said.
The Casablanca bourse all-share index closed at 641.63 points from 640.81 points Wednesday.
"The main trading was in privatisation bonds, with 27,756 bonds accounting for 71 million dirhams of the total volume traded on the official market," a broker at ABN-AMRO Finance said.
BDP1 and BDP2 were issued in January and May 1996. The first tranche closed unchanged at 1,399 dirhams, while the second fell 22 dirhams to 1,258 dirhams.
Credit firms also contributed to the rise. Credit Immobilier et Hotelier was up eight dirhams at 288 dirhams and Maroc leasing rose 12 to 415 dirhams.
In energy, oil refinery Samir rose six to 356 dirhams.
Dairy firm Centrale Laitiere gained 10 dirhams to 2,790 and edible oil company Lesieur Unigral gained 12 dirhams to 2,120 dirhams.
Among the poor performers were Morocco's largest private conglomerate, ONA, which closed at 775 dirhams, down 15.
Societe Nationale d'Investissement was unchanged at 730 dirhams.
In banking, Wafabank and Banque Marocaine pour le Commerce et de l'Industrie (BMCI) fell five dirhams each to 775 and 485 dirhams.

Total volume traded on the official market was 90.2 million dirhams compared with 26.6 million dirhams in the previous session. On the over-the-counter market, the volume was 52 million dirhams from 29.8 million dirhams. The largest trade was for 20,000 BMCI shares.
